lens: LUCK AND MULTIPLE COMPARISONS (permutation within start day / decision day / game, same-sized random subsets, family-wise max-t over the cost-cut grid, Bonferroni for 15 families / ~25 price-level variants / 522 variants, game-cluster CIs, leave-one-game-out, drop top 3 games, close-source split)
rule: R2 Plus-money only: R1 (first c/w look 2-360 min before the start with EV >= 2.5%) and implied cost < 0.50 (American above +100)
numbers_reproduced: Reproduced exactly from the loader. R2: 150 bets / 41 games; 95 with a close / 35 games; CLV +2.826% (builder 0.028256059883746715, same to 12 digits) game-cluster 95% CI [+1.97, +3.91] (builder [+1.97, +3.99]; the top differs only by bootstrap seed); close_ok 92 closes / 34 games +2.81% [+1.95, +3.95]; beat the close 79%; 66.49 bets a day. R1 (parent): 184 bets / 44 games, 116 closes / 40 games, +2.54% [+1.77, +3.52]; R1 favourites (cost >= 0.50): 34 bets, 21 closes / 14 games, +1.27%. Halves by decision day (the builder's split): Oct 3 +2.43% (16 plus closes / 13 games), Oct 4-5 +2.91% (79 / 22): matches the builder's 2.43 / 2.91. By first-look day (loader split_by_date, cut Oct 4): +2.67% (79 closes / 31 games) vs +3.58% (16 closes / 4 games). ROI at the look price -3.41% on 144 settled (builder -3.39%); at the first-listed price -3.9% [-25.7, +19.1] on 145 / 40 games: noise. Builder's luck numbers reproduced: bootstrap p(R2 <= R1 favourites) 0.006-0.007 (builder 0.008); permutation of plus-money vs random R1 closes within start/decision day p 0.056-0.059 (builder 0.060). Broad rationale reproduced: EV-adjusted cost slope -0.94 pts per +0.10 (SE 0.21, 378 closes / 59 games; builder -0.95, SE 0.22); dog minus favourite +1.57 [+1.06, +2.05].
reason: From the luck lens the rule cannot be told from chance as a RULE, although the underlying price gradient is probably not luck. (1) What R2 adds to R1 is small and borderline: R2 minus R1 mean CLV +0.28 pts per bet (95% game-cluster CI [+0.05, +0.66]); plus-money minus favourites inside R1 = +1.55 pts (SE 0.74, 21 favourite closes in 14 games vs 95 in 35). Permutation p for that gap: 0.046 (labels shuffled over all R1 closes), 0.058 (within start day), 0.058 (within decision day), 0.018 (within game); same-sized random 95-of-116 subsets of R1 closes: p 0.046 / 0.056 / 0.059 (null mean +2.55%, sd 0.16-0.17). The bootstrap p of 0.006-0.007 is the optimistic one (21 favourite closes). (2) Multiple comparisons: cut family (13 cost cuts 0.44-0.58 with >= 12 closes each side, max-t under cost-label permutation): the observed t at 0.50 (2.09) is the best of the grid, family-wise p 0.074 (no strata), 0.084 (within start day), 0.155 (within game); null median max-t 0.83-1.24, 95th percentile 2.28-2.62. The gap is not monotone in the cut: D at 0.46/0.47/0.48/0.49/0.50/0.51 = +0.66/+0.94/+1.08/+0.82/+1.55/+1.72 pts (t 0.66/1.34/1.57/1.13/2.09/1.95). Bonferroni: raw 0.046-0.058 x 15 families = 0.69-0.87; x ~25 price-level variants (20 EV-gate x price-band cells + cut variants in the builder's registry) and x 522 = 1 (capped); even the optimistic bootstrap 0.007 x 15 = 0.10. (3) The CI excluding zero ([+1.97, +3.91]) is R1's EV gate, not the price cut: R1 with no price cut is +2.54% [+1.77, +3.52]; same-sized draws from all 378 first-in-window closes (null mean +0.85%, sd 0.31) give p < 0.0002 but that only re-measures the EV >= 2.5% gate. (4) Close-source confound: 66 of R2's 95 closes (69%) are Tracker closes (56 of them CNO's own books re-read before the start, the same consensus that produced the listed EV; CLV minus listed EV = +0.1 pts there), mean +3.74%; the 26 independent closes (ESPN 4, Pinnacle 1, Novig trades with >= 3 trades 21) are +0.45% [-0.45, +1.64], p(<=0) 0.18, and Novig trades with >= 3 trades alone -0.27% (21 closes / 14 games). Within R1 only 26.5% of favourites have a Tracker close vs 44% of plus-money bets, so the source mix alone feeds the gap: with a Tracker dummy the plus-money effect falls to +0.88 (SE 0.67, p 0.20), with EV also +0.72 (SE 0.70, p 0.31); source-standardised +1.28 [+0.05, +2.96]. On independent closes inside R1 the sign is WRONG: plus +0.45% (26) vs favourites +2.15% (7), D -1.70 [-4.96, +0.62]. (5) Time: the gap lives on one game day. By decision day: Oct 3 D -0.02 [-2.30, +2.23] (16 vs 4 closes), Oct 4 +2.03 [+0.44, +4.87] (63 vs 15, 18 games), Oct 5 +0.39 [-1.74, +2.70] (16 vs 2). The builder's 'second half 2.9%' is a level on 79 closes, not evidence of a price effect; the favourite sample in the second half is 17 closes. (6) Not driven by one game but fragile to three: leave-one-game-out D +1.26 to +1.98 and level +2.66 to +3.35 over 40 games; dropping the 3 games whose removal lowers D most (three games with 2-3 closes each, 8 closes in all) leaves D +0.76 [-0.33, +2.17] on 108 closes / 37 games; dropping the 3 games that contribute most plus-money CLV leaves the level at +3.14% [+2.20, +4.04] (60 closes / 32 games), so the LEVEL is robust, the GAP is not. (7) What is probably real: the broad gradient. On all 378 first-in-window closes (59 games) dog minus favourite +1.57 [+1.06, +2.05], permutation p for the gap 0.0002 (the 5000-draw floor) globally, within start day and within game; EV-adjusted slope p 0.0002 / 0.0006 / 0.003 (global / within start day / within game); it replicates on the 262 closes NOT in R1 (53 games): +1.39 [+0.48, +2.16], slope -0.92 (SE 0.22); with close-source dummies and EV it is still +1.03 (SE 0.34, p 0.004); the gap is +1.5 to +2.0 pts at every EV gate from 0 to 3.5%. But its size by close source: Tracker +1.67 [+0.39, +3.43] (134 vs 27, circular), ESPN+Pinnacle +2.00 [+0.31, +3.60] (45 vs 24) which is partly a devig artefact (those closes use Devig.multiplicative, CNO's listed fair is the worst case of four methods; multiplicative adds +0.5 to +0.8% to a +0.45 side and subtracts 0.4 to 0.6% from a 0.55 side at 4.5% vig: a mechanical +0.9 to +1.4 pts dog-minus-favourite for a 0.45 vs 0.55 pair, about +0.7 for R1's actual 0.466 vs 0.528), and Novig trades with >= 3 trades +0.39 [-1.13, +1.52] (78 vs 42, slope -0.31, SE 0.20, p 0.13), i.e. about a third of the headline. The slope-implied gap inside R1 (mean cost 0.466 vs 0.528) is only +0.58 pts, not +1.55. (8) Cost: R2 keeps 66.5 of 81.6 R1 bets a day but CLV-units a day (bets x mean CLV) fall from 207.5 to 187.9 (-9.5%); it only pays if the daily limit binds. Verdict: the data suggests plus-money sides beat favourites against books/consensus closes, but R2 as an add-on to R1 is a +0.3 pt effect that is borderline before multiplicity (p 0.02-0.06), not significant after it (family-wise 0.07-0.16, Bonferroni-15 0.69+), resting on circular/mechanically biased closes, absent or reversed on independent closes, and present on one game day. Put to Tj only as a question (favourites need a higher EV bar), not as a recommended rule.
caveats: Only about 2.26 days of first looks and 40 games in R1 closes; 79% of R2 closes are Oct 4 games; 'second half' is Oct 4-5 decision days (or Oct 5 starts: 16 plus closes in 4 games and 2 favourite closes), too thin to check a price effect.
Only 21 favourite closes (14 games; 9 of them Tracker) carry the comparison inside R1; 34 of 184 R1 bets are favourites and 13 of them have no close.

A within-game paired comparison (9 games with both a plus-money and a favourite close, 40 vs 15 closes) is positive in all 9 games (sign-flip p 0.002; mean +4.2 pts equal-weighted, +2.9 harmonic-weighted), but 9 games is tiny, one game holds 22 of the plus closes, and the pairs mix close sources (Tracker vs Novig trades).

Permutation nulls here ignore partial within-game correlation except in the within-game version; the game-cluster bootstrap p (0.006-0.007) is optimistic for 21 favourite closes; the permutation p (0.018-0.058) is the honest range.

The 0.50 cut was declared pre-look by the builder but cannot be audited; the cut grid test assumes it was one of 13 cuts, the builder also tried cuts 0.48/0.52/0.55 and ~25 price-level variants in total (522 variants tried overall, 15 families, per the builder).

ESPN/Pinnacle closes are devigged multiplicatively (data/tracker/HistoricalCloses.kt line 167 and ParlayCloses.kt line 238), CNO's listed fair is the worst case of four methods: a CLV measured against those closes favours longshots mechanically. Tracker closes re-read CNO's own books, so CLV = listed EV + consensus drift by construction (drift +0.1 pts on plus-money Tracker closes, -1.4 on 9 favourite ones).

What would settle it: if the true gap inside R1 is the slope-implied +0.58 pts, about 10x the current data (~22 days, ~950 plus-money and ~210 favourite closes, ~400 games) for 80% power; if it is +1.55 pts about 1.4x (~3 days, 56 games); if it is the source-adjusted +0.88 about 4.4x (~10 days, ~175 games). Pinnacle (not multiplicative-devig-biased against the listing) or Novig >= 3-trade closes on the favourite side would be the decisive logging.

devig_artefact_pts.note: multiplicative minus power devig, relative fair, 4.5% vig: +0.76% at side 0.45, -0.61% at 0.55
